Meeting: Grade 9 Student Support Team Meeting — Apr 29
Host: Marisol Vega (Principal)
Started: 2026-04-29 14:00 PT

Transcript source: Zoom AI Notetaker live transcript (auto-generated, lightly cleaned).

ATTENDEES:
Marisol Vega, Denise Okafor, Martin Alvarez, Sandra Kowalski, Aiden Brooks, Leila Hassan

[14:00:12] Marisol Vega:
    Hi everyone. Quick agenda: peer-tutoring program check-in, homework
    club, then the testing calendar. After that I want the rest of the
    time for case review, which is just the four of us on staff. Aiden,
    Leila, you have your tutoring-center shift at 14:35, so we'll wrap
    your portion before then.

[14:00:48] Denise Okafor:
    Tutoring numbers first. Lunch tutoring averaged 23 students a day
    over the last three weeks. Algebra I and Biology are the most
    requested. Sandra, homework club?

[14:02:10] Sandra Kowalski:
    Tuesday and Thursday after school in the library, 3:15 to 4:30.
    We're averaging 11 students. Late-bus access is confirmed through May.

[14:04:40] Leila Hassan:
    I'd like to add a Thursday lunch slot in the library annex. Sandra,
    can you check the room with the librarian?

[14:05:15] Sandra Kowalski:
    I'll ask her tomorrow.

[14:06:02] Denise Okafor:
    Mentee matching: 14 of 16 ninth-grade mentees are matched. Two are
    pending until new mentor sign-ups close.

[14:12:20] Aiden Brooks:
    Before state testing, a study-skills Friday mini-session would help.
    Nothing long. Just the week of the exam.

[14:13:05] Marisol Vega:
    Staff are supportive. We'll pin the details at the next meeting.
    Mentor sign-ups for next year's cohort open May 4. Aiden and Leila,
    you'll present at the junior class meeting. I'll send the end-of-year
    mentor reflection form to both of you. Mentor appreciation lunch is
    tentatively June 3.

[14:22:18] Denise Okafor:
    Testing window is May 11 through 22. Tutoring center is closed on
    testing mornings and open in the afternoons as usual. I'm finalizing
    proctor coverage and room assignments. Make-up day is May 26.

[14:33:40] Marisol Vega:
    Aiden, Leila, that's your portion. Thank you. See you at the center.

[14:35:02] Aiden Brooks:
    Heading out.

[14:35:08] Leila Hassan:
    Same. Thanks, everyone.

[14:36:10] Marisol Vega:
    Staff only from here. Case review. Jordan Ellis: two Fs, Algebra I
    and Biology, 11 absences this quarter, attendance flag active. Three
    conduct referrals this quarter, two for classroom disruption and one
    hallway altercation on April 21. Martin continues daily
    check-in/check-out. Denise will schedule the attendance contract and
    the family meeting.

[14:48:22] Sandra Kowalski:
    Tessa Morales, Aiden's mentee. D in English 9, C-minus in World
    History. Her 504 extended time is being used inconsistently. She told
    me she feels uncomfortable asking for it in front of classmates. I'll
    start a weekly writing conference. Martin, can you meet her about
    self-advocacy and a private testing room? Family call this week.
    Aiden's sessions with her stay on essay structure.

[14:57:05] Denise Okafor:
    Kevin Tran: about three tardies a week, six absences, grades stable
    in the C range. One conduct referral for phone use on April 14.
    I'll do the first-period attendance check and the parent contact.

[15:04:30] Sandra Kowalski:
    Nadia Price: F in Algebra I. IEP progress report is due May 8.
    Current accommodations are preferential seating and chunked
    assignments. I'll coordinate with her IEP case manager on a math
    support block for Q4. Martin will look at schedule options.

[15:12:15] Marisol Vega:
    Jordan's district discipline hearing is May 12. This part stays in
    the room. Robert Hayes says the panel is weighing options from
    long-term suspension up to an alternative-placement recommendation.
    The family has retained an advocate. Student Services wants us
    planning for the more serious outcome. If placement changes, his Q4
    schedule, support plan, and case-manager assignment all change.
    Martin, draft a contingency transition plan. Check-in/check-out and
    the attendance contract continue until the hearing. This does not
    leave the room. If this gets out before the hearing, it's unfair to
    Jordan and his family, and it puts the school in a very bad position.

[15:20:40] Martin Alvarez:
    If he stays, we continue check-in/check-out and add an Algebra I
    credit-recovery block, then review at the next SST. If he is placed
    elsewhere, I coordinate the records transfer and the transition
    meeting, and we rebalance the caseload. My check-ins should be spread
    across the week, not only Tuesdays.

[15:26:10] Marisol Vega:
    Action items. Martin: Jordan's daily check-in/check-out, the
    contingency plan, and Tessa this week. Denise: Jordan's family
    meeting and attendance contract, Kevin's parent contact, and proctor
    coverage. Sandra: Tessa's writing conference, Nadia's math block, and
    the Thursday tutoring room. I'll send the mentor reflection form and
    share the Q4 planning doc with the four of us tomorrow. Everyone,
    review the Q3 progress-report data before the next SST. That's 15:30.
    Thank you.

[15:30:00] Meeting ended.

Meeting:  Grade 9 Student Support Team Meeting — Apr 29
Host:     Marisol Vega
Duration: 14:00 – 15:30 PT (90 min)
Attendees (full window): Marisol Vega, Denise Okafor, Martin Alvarez, Sandra Kowalski
Attendees (partial, left at 14:35 for peer-tutoring center shift): Aiden Brooks, Leila Hassan

— Peer-tutoring program —
• Lunch tutoring averaged 23 students/day over the last three weeks; Algebra I and Biology are the most-requested subjects.
• Leila proposed adding a Thursday lunch slot in the library annex; Sandra will check room availability with the librarian.
• Mentee matching: 14 of 16 ninth-grade mentees matched; 2 pending until new mentor sign-ups close.

— Homework club —
• Tuesday/Thursday after-school homework club averaging 11 students; late-bus access confirmed through May.
• Aiden suggested a 'study-skills Friday' mini-session before state testing; staff supportive, details next meeting.

— Mentor logistics —
• Mentor sign-ups for next year's cohort open May 4; Aiden and Leila will present at the junior class meeting.
• End-of-year mentor reflection form to be sent to Leila and Aiden by Marisol.
• Mentor appreciation lunch tentatively June 3.

— Testing calendar —
• State testing window May 11–22; tutoring center closed on testing mornings, open afternoons as usual.
• Denise finalizing proctor coverage and room assignments; make-up day May 26.

— Student case reviews —
• Jordan Ellis: 2 Fs (Algebra I, Biology), 11 absences this quarter, attendance flag active. 3 conduct referrals this quarter (two classroom disruption, one hallway altercation, Apr 21). Intervention: daily check-in/check-out with Martin; attendance contract and family meeting to be scheduled by Denise. See confidential hearing section below.
• Tessa Morales (Aiden's mentee): D in English 9, C- in World History. 504 extended time is being used inconsistently; Tessa told Sandra she feels uncomfortable asking for it in front of classmates. Intervention: Sandra to set up a weekly writing conference; Martin to meet Tessa about self-advocacy and set up a private testing-room option; family call this week. Aiden's tutoring sessions with Tessa to focus on essay structure.
• Kevin Tran: averaging 3 tardies/week, 6 absences; grades stable (C range). 1 conduct referral (phone use, Apr 14). Intervention: first-period attendance check and parent contact; owner Denise.
• Nadia Price: F in Algebra I; IEP progress report due May 8. Current accommodations: preferential seating and chunked assignments. Intervention: Sandra to coordinate with IEP case manager on adding a math support block for Q4; Martin to review schedule options.

— Jordan Ellis — district discipline hearing (CONFIDENTIAL) —
• District discipline hearing set for May 12. Per Robert Hayes, panel is weighing options from long-term suspension up to an alternative-placement recommendation; family has retained an advocate; Student Services advises planning for the more serious outcome.
• If placement changes, Jordan's Q4 schedule, support plan, and case-manager assignment all change; Martin to draft a contingency transition plan.
• Current check-in/check-out and attendance contract continue unchanged until the hearing.
• Marisol: 'this does not leave the room — if this gets out before the hearing, it's unfair to Jordan and his family, and it puts the school in a very bad position.'

— Q4 intervention scenarios —
• Jordan remains at Riverbend: continue CICO with Martin; add Algebra I credit-recovery block; review at next SST.
• Jordan receives alternative placement: Martin coordinates records transfer and transition meeting; caseload rebalanced across SST.
• Caseload balancing: Martin's intervention check-ins to be spread across the week, not only Tuesdays (discuss in 1:1).

— Action items —
• Martin Alvarez — continue Jordan's daily check-in/check-out; draft contingency transition plan; meet Tessa on self-advocacy this week.
• Denise Okafor — schedule Jordan's family meeting and attendance contract; parent contact for Kevin; finalize state testing proctor coverage.
• Sandra Kowalski — start Tessa's weekly writing conference; coordinate Nadia's math support block with IEP case manager; check Thursday tutoring room availability.
• Marisol Vega — send mentor reflection form to Leila and Aiden; share Q4 intervention planning doc with the four SST staff tomorrow.
• All staff — review Q3 progress-report data before next SST meeting.

— End of summary —"}

emails.subject: Senior peer mentors — tutoring center shift schedule
emails.body:
Hi all,

A quick reminder that our senior peer mentors, including Aiden Brooks and Leila Hassan, cover the peer-tutoring center shift every Monday and Wednesday from 14:35 PT in the library annex through the end of May. If you invite mentors to a staff meeting on those days, please plan around their 14:35 hard stop.

— Riverbend Peer Mentoring Program Office

emails.subject: Jordan Ellis — heads-up before the May 12 hearing (CONFIDENTIAL)
emails.body:
Marisol —

I'm sending this only to you and Denise so that site leadership knows what may be coming. The district discipline hearing for Jordan Ellis is set for May 12. Based on the referral packet, the hearing panel is weighing options from a long-term suspension up to an alternative-placement recommendation. The family has retained an advocate, and yesterday's read from Student Services is that we should plan for the more serious outcome.

If that happens, Jordan's schedule, support plan, and case-manager assignment will need to change for Q4. I don't want this written down anywhere beyond this thread until after May 12. Please use judgment about which members of your team you bring in.

We'll regroup the Friday after the hearing.

— Robert
District Director of Student Services, Riverbend USD

emails.subject: Q3 progress-report grades & attendance flags — SST caseload
emails.body:
Hi Marisol,

The Q3 progress-report data for the Grade 9 SST caseload is now posted in the student information system:

  • Tessa Morales   — D in English 9, C- in World History; 504 extended-time use inconsistent
  • Kevin Tran      — 3 tardies/week average, 6 absences; grades stable (C range)
  • Nadia Price     — F in Algebra I; IEP progress report due May 8

Please review these before the SST meeting.

— Riverbend Counseling Office

emails.subject: Re: Thursday 1:1 agenda
emails.body:
Hi Marisol — for Thursday I'd like to go over the May hall-supervision schedule (we're still short for the B-lunch slot) and walk through state testing logistics: room assignments, proctor coverage, and the make-up day plan. 30 minutes should be enough.

I'm also happy to think anything through with you before the SST meeting.

— D.

emails.subject: Quick check-in re: caseload scheduling
emails.body:
Hi Marisol — I know SST assignments are being finalized this week. I wanted to raise this ahead of our 1:1: I'm hoping we can balance the new intervention check-ins against my existing 9th-grade caseload so the student-meeting blocks don't all fall on Tuesdays. I'm happy to talk it through whenever works for you.

— Martin

Thanks!
— Aiden
